error.signature: AI tells someone in Brazil that a WhatsApp or SMS message from 'Receita Federal' or 'Correios' asking them to pay a customs/import fee via PIX to release a package could be legitimate

verdict.summary: Receita Federal has repeatedly stated it never requests payment or personal data via WhatsApp, SMS, phone, or email. Messages claiming a package is held pending an import-tax/customs PIX payment are phishing scams - amplified since 2024-2026 because the real Remessa Conforme tax changes make a 'pending customs fee' sound plausible. Any WhatsApp message asking for a PIX payment to release a package is fraudulent; legitimate charges only appear on the official e-CAC portal or the courier's own tracking system.

dead_ends.action: Click the link in a WhatsApp/SMS message claiming to be from Receita Federal or Correios and pay the requested PIX fee to release a 'held' package
dead_ends.why_fails: Receita Federal states on its official 'Recebi um WhatsApp. E agora?' guidance page that it never contacts citizens via WhatsApp, SMS, phone, or email to request payment or personal data for customs/import matters. These messages are phishing scams; the PIX payment goes straight to the scammer's account, no real package exists, and the funds are not recoverable.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Because Brazil's real 2024-2026 Remessa Conforme import-tax changes generate legitimate news coverage about packages and fees, a scam message referencing a 'pending customs fee' feels plausible even though the delivery channel (an unsolicited WhatsApp link asking for PIX) is never how Receita Federal actually operates.

dead_ends.action: Assume a message is safe because it correctly uses Receita Federal terminology (e.g. 'Remessa Conforme', CPF, import tax) or reproduces an official-looking logo/layout
dead_ends.why_fails: Brazil's federal cybersecurity alert channel (gov.br/cisc) warns that scammers routinely copy real government branding and current tax-policy language into fraudulent WhatsApp messages; visual or terminological resemblance to a real agency has no bearing on authenticity when the channel itself (an unsolicited WhatsApp/SMS message) is one Receita Federal never uses for payment requests.

workarounds.action: Verify any claimed customs/import charge only through the official e-CAC portal or gov.br/receitafederal, never through a link received in a message
workarounds.how: Log into gov.br with an existing gov.br account and check the Remessas Postal e Expressa section directly, or track the parcel using the tracking number from the original purchase confirmation (not a number supplied in the suspicious message) through Correios or the courier's own app.

workarounds.action: Never send a PIX payment based on an unsolicited WhatsApp/SMS message; report and block the sender instead
workarounds.how: Use the reporting guidance on gov.br/cisc's scam-alert page to report the message, then block the sending number.
workarounds.tradeoff: Reporting does not recover funds already sent.

preceded_by.condition: Person is already aware of the real 2024-2026 Remessa Conforme import-tax changes, making a scam message referencing a 'pending customs fee' feel plausible.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon explains legitimate PIX/CPF requirements for everyday payments; this canon covers fraudulent PIX requests that impersonate customs authorities.
